Nilüfer Hoca's strongest points are, she takes her work very seriously, and expects the same from her students. A person who will take this class to learn and improve their English, both in terms of speaking and writing will surely be highly satisfied with her course. She grades fairly, and states her grading criteria and expectations quite detailed in an understandable way. If you are a person who is easy to get along with, open to learning, and activite at participating, she will value your presence in the class. She distinguishes effort and expresses her appreciation, and her positive motivation made me even more interested in her class and I truly wanted to learn how to write more academic essays, and how to do better presentations. She herself being a successful and hardworking student once, empathizes more with such students, which is something I would recommend to everyone, apart from building a stronger connection with Nilüfer Hoca. 
As for weak aspects, I cannot find it in myself yet to be finding out her weak aspects as she is a very sophisticated and responsible instructor. However, I can call what I'll be explaining now as improvable areas, for even more instructive future courses. I believe discussing the course readings (their content and counter arguments) as a whole class would be more efficient as it would give all students strong ideas on what they can write about and which stance they will choose in certain topics in their essays. In our class, we mostly did these in groups, understandably, students were sometimes quite uninterested for their own reasons. Therefore, if it is possible to implement this into the course, it would be a great addition.

course: In all honesty, I am disappointed that this course was a mandatory course in my curriculum. This is an English Grammar course where the linguistic terminology of grammatical structures are taught. It does not help us to improve our English skills – writing, speaking etc. – and is not related to the curriculum of the literature departments. It may only be beneficial to those who’d wish to choose a path in language education. Yet, this course is mandatory for every ELIT and AMER student for TWO SEMESTERS. I do not understand Bilkent’s purpose in having this course as a mandatory course in our curriculum. I wish this was offered as an elective instead so that those who do not plan to take the “language education” career path could spend their time taking other courses that would add to their literary studies. Or possibly this course’s objectives could be changed so drastically that we’d learn the linguistic development of the English language in historical context so that it would in some way benefit our literature education. Its current state of functioning as JUST a grammar course is quite disappointing coming from Bilkent, or perhaps this course has some other benefits that are beyond my comprehension.
